 In 2026, Aryna Sabalenka wore $330,000 worth of jewelry to win the US Open; Now she’s a luxury brand’s first ambassador
 Originally posted on
 Athlon Sports 
  | 
 By Faizan Mirza
  | 
 Last updated Nov 9, 2026 2:40 PM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 Aryna Sabalenka’s US Open 2026 jewelry was noteworthy. Now, the tennis champ is the luxury jeweler Material Good’s first ambassador.
 But a new door has been opened in the luxury world for Aryna Sabalenka’s success on the tennis courts. The Belarusian is the first-ever jewelry ambassador for Material Good, a jeweler based in New York.
 The partnership officially kicked off in 2026 with Sabalenka making her ambassador debut at the Australian Open. It also was the start of a partnership with the world’s No. 1 that will allow her to get to know how to craft garments she can wear on the court and off.
 How Aryna Sabalenka’s $330,000 Jewelry Made Headlines
 Sabalenka has been a Material Good ambassador since she found the brand in the middle of her 2025 US Open campaign. She had three custom pieces during the tournament: diamond drop earrings, a tourmaline pendant, and a diamond choker.
 Aryna Sabalenka reacts during Women’s Singles Fourth Round match on Day Eight of the 2026 US Open.(Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)
 All of the designs featured a personal element, and the number eight was included in each to mark her eighth visit to Flushing Meadows. The pendant contained a special 10.72-carat pink-orange tourmaline, and the choker was adorned with seven diamonds in the shape of a pear and an imperial topaz.
 The $330,000 amount, however, is for an estimated three-piece Material Good collection Sabalenka wore during the 2026 US Open. This jeweler’s set consisted of a necklace, bracelet, and earrings, valued at about $110,000 each. This was a non-disclosed price.
 Aryna Sabalenka Becomes Material Good’s First Ambassador
 After Sabalenka’s natural connection that evolved since the US Open in 2025, it was a no-brainer that she would be a natural fit for Material Good’s first-ever jewelry ambassador.
 The collaboration doesn’t end with wearing the brand’s wear. Sabalenka collaborates with her designers to create custom pieces for her tennis wardrobe that won’t hinder her movement on the court.
 View this post on Instagram 
 “Jewelry is a way that I express myself, both on and off the court, and this partnership felt like a natural next step in my style evolution,” Sabalenka said. 
 Sabalenka’s passion for jewelry has become a part of her burgeoning personal brand, whether it’s the Grand Slam win or the formal luxury partnership.
